options: A required cloud service that Git cannot function without
A type of branch that cannot be deleted
The name of your current working directory
Another copy of the repository your local repository can communicate with
questions.explain: A remote is simply another copy of the repository Git knows how to talk to — it could be GitHub, a teammate's machine, or a company server. Git itself doesn't require any particular hosting service.

questions.q: What does git fetch do that git pull does not?
options: fetch deletes your local branches; pull does not
fetch uploads your commits to the remote; pull does not
fetch downloads new remote commits without merging them into your current branch; pull merges them in automatically
There is no difference between fetch and pull
questions.explain: git fetch only updates Git's record of what the remote has (e.g. origin/main) without touching your working directory; git pull does a fetch and then immediately merges the new commits into your current branch.

questions.q: What is the conventional name Git uses for the remote a repository was cloned from?
options: origin
master
source
root
questions.explain: "origin" is the conventional name git clone assigns to the remote it cloned from — a convention, not a hard rule enforced by Git itself.

questions.q: What happens if you git push a branch to the remote, and the remote branch already has commits your local branch doesn't?
options: Git silently overwrites the remote's commits with yours
The push is rejected until you reconcile the two by fetching/pulling first
Git automatically deletes the remote branch
Nothing — push always succeeds regardless
questions.explain: Git refuses a push that would overwrite commits it doesn't know about on the remote, forcing you to fetch/pull and reconcile the histories first.

options: Creates a new empty repository with no history
Only downloads the current branch's latest commit
Downloads a full copy of a repository's entire history and sets up its remote automatically
Merges two existing local repositories together
questions.explain: git clone downloads the complete history of a repository, not just the current files, and automatically configures origin to point back at where it came from.
